column1: # Dev-log entries whose version is verified by CONTAINMENT rather than by being
# ahead of every release.
# tools/devlog-entry-version-guard.sh checks that a newly added entry names a
# build that has not shipped yet. That is the right rule for an authored entry,
# whose version is a prediction. It is the wrong rule for CORRECTING an entry
# that is already on main and already carries the wrong number: the fix gives it
# the number of a release that has necessarily already happened, which the
# forward-looking rule refuses.
# An entry listed here is measured against the stronger property instead — the
# release it names must be the FIRST release containing the commit the entry
# describes. That is proven from the tags, not asserted, so a listing cannot
# wave a wrong number through; it can only substitute one machine-checked proof
# for another. Anything not listed here keeps the forward-looking rule untouched.
# The anchor is the commit whose change the entry describes, NOT the commit that
# added the entry file: every entry file's add-commit is the one-file-per-entry
# migration, which says nothing about when the change shipped.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   <entry path>
# Use a full 40-character SHA: an abbreviation can become ambiguous as history
# grows, and the guard fails closed rather than guessing.
client/devlog/0.60.0.json
column3: Describes the guarded grounded walk gait, which first shipped in v0.60.0. The entry was authored as 0.59.0 and a sibling release was cut ahead of it, so it named a build released before the code existed (#435).
